title: Raise TermAl's Engram call deadline above Engram's 60 s control-request allowance (to 90 s), so Engram's typed expiry or busy refusals arrive before the host gives up
outcome:
Requested by Engram::Opus (TermAl mailbox 587a65fb #522, 2026-11-23 06:48Z) for Engram w-8f127d78e960 R1, where both reviewers (Codex 19682, Claude 19683, on a90d1fad) found the same Medium.
The mismatch:
- Engram's CONTROL_REQUEST_ALLOWANCE is now 60 s, measured from the frame's first byte.
- TermAl's ENGRAM_MAX_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS = ENGRAM_DEFAULT_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000 (src/engram_host_adapter.rs:22-23) is measured from the send, so under 60 s of store contention TermAl always times out first.
- TermAl then sees an UNKNOWN outcome needing exact-key reconciliation, instead of Engram's typed `control_request_expired` (nothing committed; retry the same key) or `control_startup_busy` (re-admission permitted).
Engram's side, in its own item: control startup shares one 60 s window across all its waits.
TermAl's side, this item: raise the host-side Engram call deadline (max and default) to 90 s. That respects Greg's rule of no abort under 60 s with a 10 s warning, and lets Engram's typed refusals at 60 s reach TermAl.
Constraints:
- The 60 s operation minimum in scripts/engram-call-budget-ms.json, shared with the launcher, and the 10 s warning are unchanged unless a caller's budget arithmetic requires otherwise.
- Every budget that sums call timeouts (for example src/acceptance_evaluation_api.rs:29-96) is reviewed for the larger value.
acceptance: TermAl's deadline for an ordinary Engram control call is 90 s (maximum and default), the slow-call warning stays at 10 s, and no Engram call is aborted before 60 s.

When Engram answers a control call with a typed control_request_expired or control_startup_busy refusal after 60 s and before 90 s, TermAl reports that typed outcome instead of an unknown timeout; a deterministic behaviour test with an injected clock or fake transport covers both, with no real-time waits.
Every budget that adds Engram call timeouts (acceptance evaluation and evidence recovery among them) remains consistent with the new deadline, and the change of each is recorded on the item.
